summary: Raghunath Giri was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Bama Charan Bhattacharya. He taught Atsushi Uno and held the position of department head (科長) at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Rahul Peter Das is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the universities of Calcutta, Cologne, and Hamburg under Klaus Ludwig Janert and Albrecht Wezler. He served as Chair and Professor of South Asian Studies at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg.

Rahul Sankrityayan (1893–1963) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He taught Sanskrit at Vidyalankara Pirivena in 1927 and served as a Sanskrit teacher and professor at Saint Petersburg State University in 1937 and from 1945 to 1947.

Raimo Anttila (1935–2023) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Yale University under Warren Crawford Cowgill. He held academic posts at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1965 and the University of Helsinki from 1971 to 1976.

Raimon Panikkar (1918–2010) studied at Barcelona, Bonn, Complutense University of Madrid under Juan Zaragüeta, Pontifical Lateran University, Mysore, and Banaras Hindu University. He held teaching posts at Complutense, Harvard, and UC Santa Barbara.

Raimond Gaita is a philosopher who studied at the University of Melbourne and the University of Leeds. He served as Professor of Moral Philosophy at King's College London (1977–2011) and Foundation Professor of Philosophy at Australian Catholic University (1993–2011).

Historian and Indologist Rajan Gurukkal studied at the University of Calicut and Jawaharlal Nehru University. He was the Director of the School of Social Sciences at Mahatma Gandhi University (1988) and Sundararajan Visiting Professor at the Indian Institute of Science (2012–2016).
Rajat Verma works in the fields of computational studies and Indology, holding posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi and BharatGen.

Rajeev Sangal works in computational linguistics and Indology, having studied at IIT Kanpur and the University of Pennsylvania. He held posts at IIT Kanpur, IIIT Hyderabad (including as professor from 2002 to 2013), and IIT (BHU) Varanasi.

Rajendra Chandra Hazra (1904–1982) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Dhaka under Sushil Kumar De. He taught at Jagannath University and the University of Dhaka, and was Associate Professor of Smṛti and Purāṇa at Sanskrit College.

Indologist Rajendra Mishra studied under traditional teacher Rāmbhadrācārya. He served as head of the Sanskrit department at Himachal Pradesh University, visiting professor at the University of Indonesia, and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Rajendralal Mitra (1824–1891) was an Indologist and historian who studied at the Medical College and Hospital and the University of Calcutta. He served as librarian-cum-assistant-secretary and later president of the Asiatic Society, and directed the Wards' Institution.

Rajkrishna Mukhopadhyay (1845–1886) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Krishnagar Government College and Presidency College, Kolkata, and later held teaching posts at Scottish Church College and Presidency College.

Rakhal Das Banerji (1885–1930) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta. He served as an officer in the Archaeological Survey of India and held the Manindra Chandra Nandy professorship at Banaras Hindu University.
Rakra Tethong Rinpoche studied under Gendün Chöphel and Trijang Rinpoche.

Ralf Kramer studied Tibetology and Buddhist studies at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and at the University of London. Between approximately 2004 and 2011, he served as the Aris Librarian for Tibetan & Himalayan Studies at the Bodleian Library.

Ralph Abraham (1936–2024) studied at the University of Michigan and under Debabrata SenSharma. He held posts at UC Berkeley, Columbia, and Princeton before serving as associate professor (1968) and professor (1980) at the University of California, Santa Cruz.

Ralph Lerner is a philosopher who studied at the University of Chicago between 1944 and 1953 under Leo Strauss. He subsequently held a faculty post at the University of Chicago from roughly 1953 to 2003.

Ralph Lilley Turner (1888–1983) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Christ's College, Cambridge. He held a professorship at Banaras Hindu University and was a professor at the University of London and director of SOAS from 1922 to 1957.

Ralph T. H. Griffith (1826–1906) was an Indologist who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford, under Horace Hayman Wilson. He served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit in 1849 and was Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from approximately 1861 to 1876.
